title: Possession with عِنْدَ and لِـ
lede: Say who has something, who it belongs to and who physically has it with them—without forcing one English “have” structure onto every Arabic meaning.

items.feedback: عِنْدِي is the common possession pattern “with me / I have”.
لِي marks belonging or allocation: the book is mine.

items.prompt: Which form means “you have” to one female?
items.feedback: The attached pronoun matches the person addressed.
لِمَنْ asks ownership or allocation.

items.prompt: Which phrase means “with me/on my person”?
items.feedback: مَعِي often means the item is physically with the speaker, not simply owned.

items.prompt: In عِنْدِي كِتَابٌ, what case is the item normally in a fully marked model?
items.feedback: The delayed noun/topic is normally nominative: كِتَابٌ.
ـنَا gives “with us / we have”.
The dual pronoun ending is ـهُمَا.

items.prompt: Choose “you have” for a feminine plural group.
items.feedback: ـكُنَّ addresses a feminine plural group.
عِنْدَهَا marks a feminine possessor; the item is nominative with its adjective.

items.prompt: Choose “This seat is for you” to one male.
items.feedback: لَكَ marks allocation or belonging to one male.

items.prompt: Choose “The decision is theirs” for a masculine/mixed group.
items.feedback: لَهُمْ means “for/belonging to them”.
لَنَا marks ownership or allocation.
The standard combined form is لِي.
عِنْدِي naturally expresses availability or possession.
لِي focuses on assignment or belonging.

items.prompt: Choose “I have the keys with me.”
items.feedback: مَعِي says the keys are physically with the speaker.

items.prompt: Which sentence can mean “I own a car” in neutral everyday Arabic?
items.feedback: عِنْدِي is the ordinary possession pattern; context can show ownership or availability.

items.prompt: Choose “I do not have a pen.”
items.feedback: لَيْسَ عِنْدِي is a clear standard MSA negation of possession.

items.prompt: Choose “Do you have a question?” to one female.
items.feedback: Use هَلْ + عِنْدَكِ for one female listener.
لِمَنْ directly asks ownership.
لَهَا answers ownership; pronoun reference makes the owned item understood.

items.prompt: Choose “They have two children” for a dual owner.
items.feedback: عِنْدَهُمَا marks two owners; the possessed item is nominative dual.
عِنْدَنَا expresses possession/availability; the item and adjective are nominative.

items.prompt: Choose “This office is for the manager.”
items.feedback: لِـ marks allocation or belonging; it contracts with الـ to لِلـ.
مَعِي focuses on present physical accompaniment.

options: مَا لِي وَقْتٌ is the only standard form
items.feedback: لَيْسَ عِنْدِي is a clear functional standard form.
لِمَنْ asks who owns or is assigned the books.

items.prompt: Choose “These books are theirs” for a feminine plural group.
items.feedback: لَهُنَّ marks feminine plural ownership.

items.prompt: Which sentence means “She has her passport with her”?
items.feedback: مَعَهَا focuses on physical possession at that moment.

options: عِنْدَ, لِـ and مَعَ express related but different relationships
items.feedback: Choose according to possession/availability, belonging/allocation or physical accompaniment.

options: عِنْدِي حَاسُوبٌ، وَلَكِنَّ هَذَا الْهَاتِفَ لِأَخِي، وَمَفَاتِيحُهُ مَعِي.
عِنْدِي حَاسُوبًا، وَلَكِنَّ هَذَا الْهَاتِفُ عِنْدَ أَخِي لِي.
items.feedback: The sentence uses each possession marker for its natural relationship and keeps case accurate.

games.feedback: عِنْدَهَا is the neutral possession pattern.
مَعَهَا says she has them on her person/with her now.

games.prompt: Do you have time? — one female
games.feedback: Use هَلْ عِنْدَكِ for ordinary availability.

games.prompt: We do not have a lesson today
games.feedback: لَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا is a clear standard negative possession pattern.

games.prompt: This room is for the students
games.feedback: لِـ marks allocation or intended use.

blocks: ## Arabic expresses “have” through relationships
Instead of relying on one verb equivalent to English “have”, Arabic often locates an item with someone or marks it as belonging to someone.
[ar] عِنْدِي قَلَمٌ.
[ar] هَذَا الْقَلَمُ لِي.
[ar] الْقَلَمُ مَعِي.
[ar] عِنْدَهَا فِكْرَةٌ جَيِّدَةٌ.
[callout] Communication first: choose the structure that matches the relationship—availability, ownership, allocation or physical accompaniment.
## Choose your route
Build عِنْدَ and لِـ forms, then learn when each one is natural.
### Core
- Use عِنْدِي, عِنْدَكَ and عِنْدَهُ in short possession statements.
- Use لِي, لَكَ and لَهُ for belonging.
- Ask and answer simple possession questions.
### Develop
- Control the complete pronoun families.
- Negate possession and use dual/plural items.
- Distinguish عِنْدَ, لِـ and مَعَ.
### Stretch
- Analyse case in delayed possessed nouns.
- Use allocation and abstract possession precisely.
- Edit extended answers for natural choice and reference.
## Readiness check
Choose the marker that matches “have”, “belongs to” or “is with”.
## عِنْدَ + pronoun: possession and availability
The locator عِنْدَ combines with pronoun endings to mean “at/with someone” and commonly “someone has”.

TABLE: Person | Form | Model // I | عِنْدِي | عِنْدِي سُؤَالٌ. // we | عِنْدَنَا | عِنْدَنَا وَقْتٌ. // you m. sg. | عِنْدَكَ | هَلْ عِنْدَكَ قَلَمٌ؟ // you f. sg. | عِنْدَكِ | هَلْ عِنْدَكِ فِكْرَةٌ؟ // you dual | عِنْدَكُمَا | عِنْدَكُمَا كِتَابَانِ. // you m./mixed pl. | عِنْدَكُمْ | عِنْدَكُمْ أَسْئِلَةٌ. // you f. pl. | عِنْدَكُنَّ | عِنْدَكُنَّ مَوْعِدٌ. // he | عِنْدَهُ | عِنْدَهُ سَيَّارَةٌ. // she | عِنْدَهَا | عِنْدَهَا أُخْتَانِ. // they dual | عِنْدَهُمَا | عِنْدَهُمَا طِفْلَانِ. // they m./mixed pl. | عِنْدَهُمْ | عِنْدَهُمْ مَشْرُوعٌ. // they f. pl. | عِنْدَهُنَّ | عِنْدَهُنَّ حِصَّةٌ.

[callout] Case pattern: in a fully marked model, the possessed item is normally nominative as the delayed topic: عِنْدِي كِتَابٌ , عِنْدِي سَيَّارَتَانِ , عِنْدِي كُتُبٌ . The pronoun after عِنْدَ is the relational complement.
## لِـ + noun or pronoun: belonging and allocation
The preposition لِـ marks who something belongs to, is intended for, or is allocated to.

TABLE: Person | Combined form | Model // me | لِي | هَذَا لِي. // us | لَنَا | هَذَا الْمَشْرُوعُ لَنَا. // you m. sg. | لَكَ | هَذَا الْمَقْعَدُ لَكَ. // you f. sg. | لَكِ | هَذِهِ الرِّسَالَةُ لَكِ. // you dual | لَكُمَا | هَذَانِ الْكِتَابَانِ لَكُمَا. // you m./mixed pl. | لَكُمْ | هَذَا الْوَقْتُ لَكُمْ. // you f. pl. | لَكُنَّ | هَذِهِ الْغُرْفَةُ لَكُنَّ. // him | لَهُ | الْقَلَمُ لَهُ. // her | لَهَا | السَّيَّارَةُ لَهَا. // them dual | لَهُمَا | الْبَيْتُ لَهُمَا. // them m./mixed pl. | لَهُمْ | الْقَرَارُ لَهُمْ. // them f. pl. | لَهُنَّ | الْكُتُبُ لَهُنَّ.
Before a definite noun, لِـ joins the article and the alif is omitted in spelling: لِلْمُعَلِّمِ , لِلطُّلَّابِ . With the first-person suffix, the standard form is لِي .
## Choose by meaning: عِنْدَ, لِـ or مَعَ
The three structures overlap in English translation but focus on different relationships.

TABLE: Intended meaning | Best core structure | Example // someone has / something is available to them | عِنْدَ | عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ. // something belongs to / is allocated to someone | لِـ | هَذَا الْمَكْتَبُ لِي. // something is physically with someone now | مَعَ | جَوَازُ السَّفَرِ مَعِي.
[ar] عِنْدِي سَيَّارَةٌ.
[ar] السَّيَّارَةُ لِي.
[ar] السَّيَّارَةُ مَعِي الْيَوْمَ.
[ar] عِنْدِي فِكْرَةٌ، وَلَكِنَّ الْقَرَارَ لِلْمُدِيرِ.
## Questions and negation
Possession becomes useful when learners can ask, deny, clarify and correct.

TABLE: Purpose | Pattern | Example // Ask whether someone has something | هَلْ عِنْدَ + pronoun + item | هَلْ عِنْدَكِ سُؤَالٌ؟ // Ask what someone has | مَاذَا عِنْدَ + pronoun | مَاذَا عِنْدَكُمْ؟ // Ask ownership | لِمَنْ + item | لِمَنْ هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَةُ؟ // Answer ownership | item + لِـ + pronoun | هِيَ لَهَا. // Negate possession | لَيْسَ عِنْدَ + pronoun + item | لَيْسَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ. // Negate ownership | item + لَيْسَ لِـ + pronoun / لَيْسَ item لِـ | هَذَا الْكِتَابُ لَيْسَ لِي.

[callout/warning] Do not use bare لَا before عِنْدَ as the default formal pattern. For clear MSA, use لَيْسَ عِنْدِي... or a suitable verbal alternative such as لَا أَمْلِكُ... when literal ownership is intended.
## Number and agreement of the possessed item
The owner marker stays fixed while the item changes for gender and number.

TABLE: Item type | Model | What to notice // Masculine singular | عِنْدَهَا قَلَمٌ جَدِيدٌ. | item and adjective nominative masculine // Feminine singular | عِنْدَهُ سَيَّارَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ. | item and adjective nominative feminine // Dual | عِنْدَهُمَا طِفْلَانِ. | nominative dual // Human masculine plural | عِنْدَنَا مُعَلِّمُونَ مُخْلِصُونَ. | full human plural agreement // Non-human plural | عِنْدِي كُتُبٌ مُفِيدَةٌ. | feminine singular adjective
The pronoun inside عِنْدَهَا identifies the owner. It does not force the possessed noun to be feminine; the item keeps its own gender and number.
## Combine all three possession systems
Strong answers switch naturally among suffixes, iḍāfa, عِنْدَ and لِـ.

عِنْدِي حَاسُوبٌ مَحْمُولٌ أَسْتَخْدِمُهُ لِلدِّرَاسَةِ، وَلَكِنَّ هَذَا الْهَاتِفَ لِأَخِي. جَوَازُ سَفَرِهِ مَعِي الْيَوْمَ لِأَنَّنَا سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَطَارِ. عِنْدَ أُخْتِي تَذْكِرَتَانِ، وَحَقِيبَتَاهَا فِي السَّيَّارَةِ.
- Find one possessive suffix.
- Find one iḍāfa.
- Find عِنْدَ for possession.
- Find لِـ for ownership/purpose.
- Find مَعَ for physical accompaniment.
[callout] Range with purpose: variety is valuable when each structure carries a different relationship. Do not replace a natural simple form merely to sound complex.
## Proofreading clinic
Choose the possession structure before checking pronouns, case and agreement.

TABLE: Draft | Improved version | Reason // أَنَا عِنْدِي قَلَمٌ. | عِنْدِي قَلَمٌ. | The independent pronoun is usually unnecessary unless contrast is intended. // عِنْدِي قَلَمًا. | عِنْدِي قَلَمٌ. | The possessed item is normally nominative in the basic pattern. // هَذَا الْكِتَابُ عِنْدِي. (meaning: it belongs to me) | هَذَا الْكِتَابُ لِي. | Use لِي for explicit ownership. // عِنْدِي الْمَفَاتِيحُ مَعِي. | الْمَفَاتِيحُ مَعِي. / عِنْدِي الْمَفَاتِيحُ. | Choose the intended focus; avoid redundant stacking. // لِإِي هَذَا الْمَقْعَدُ. | هَذَا الْمَقْعَدُ لِي. | The combined first-person form is لِي and the normal order starts with the item. // لَا عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ. | لَيْسَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ. | Use a clear standard negative pattern. // عِنْدَهَا كِتَابٌ جَدِيدَةٌ. | عِنْدَهَا كِتَابٌ جَدِيدٌ. | The adjective matches the item, not the owner.
## Game: Whose, who has, or who carries?
Choose عِنْدَ, لِـ or مَعَ according to the intended relationship.
## Skills workshop
Ask about belongings, explain ownership and keep reference clear.
### Role-play: lost property
Ask who has an item, whose it is and whether it is physically with the person now. Use at least four forms from:
هَلْ عِنْدَكَ...؟ لِمَنْ هَذَا؟ هَلْ هُوَ لَكَ؟ هَلْ هُوَ مَعَكَ الآنَ؟
### Reading: allocation notice
الْغُرْفَةُ الْأُولَى لِلطُّلَّابِ، وَالثَّانِيَةُ لِلطَّالِبَاتِ. عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَجْمُوعَةٍ مِفْتَاحٌ، وَالْبِطَاقَاتُ مَعَ الْمُشْرِفَةِ.
Explain the different relationship expressed by each possession marker.
### Ownership, availability and responsibility
Write 110–130 Arabic words about belongings and responsibilities in a home, class, journey, event or workplace.
[callout] Success checklist: Use four عِنْدَ forms, four لِـ forms, two مَعَ forms, two questions, one negative, one dual/plural item, two possessive suffixes and two iḍāfa phrases.
[callout] Paper route: Create three columns headed “has/available”, “belongs/allocated” and “physically with”. Sort your ideas before writing.
## Final mastery check
Show that you can distinguish possession, belonging and accompaniment.
### You can now
- Use the complete عِنْدَ and لِـ pronoun families.
- Ask and answer ownership questions.
- Negate possession clearly.
- Distinguish عِنْدَ, لِـ and مَعَ.
- Keep the possessed item’s number and agreement accurate.
- Combine possession markers with suffixes and iḍāfa in connected language.
Spaced revisit: rewrite a previous home, school or travel paragraph and replace repeated ownership language with the most precise possession structure.
